final_message:
Fixed. The bug was in `mrr` in `billing/reports.py`. It filtered subscriptions with `subscription["customer_id"] not in ("active", "past_due")`, so every subscription was skipped. It now checks `subscription["status"]`.

I added your reproduction test to `tests/test_reports.py` with the missing `reports` import. The full suite passes (25 tests). The aging half of the test already passed once MRR was right.

I also wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && wc -l reports.py && cat reports.py

cd .. && sed -i 's/if subscription\["customer_id"\] not in ("active", "past_due")/if subscription["status"] not in ("active", "past_due")/' billing/reports.py && echo '{"file": "reports.py", "function": "mrr"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cd .. && cat >> tests/test_reports.py <<'EOF'


def test_mrr_and_aging(world):
    from billing import catalog

    yearly = catalog.create_price(world.ctx, world.plan["id"], "usd", "flat", unit_amount=12000, interval="year")
    a = world.customer()
    b = world.customer(email="b@example.com", card=False)
    world.engine.subscribe(a["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 3)])
    world.engine.subscribe(b["id"], [(yearly["id"], 1)])
    assert reports.mrr(world.ctx) == {"usd": 3000 + 1000}
    world.clock.advance_days(40)
    aging = reports.aging(world.ctx, world.clock.now())
    assert aging["usd"]["31-60"] == 12000
EOF
ls tests; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15

cd . && sed -i '' '1i\
from billing import reports\
\
' tests/test_reports.py && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15
